text:
kevin: quick sync — i pushed a proposal for a lightweight gating layer for the checkpoint resolver. goal: decouple namespace resolution from hotstart warmup and make fallback behavior explicit. link: https://r.rw/rfc-checkpoint-resolver-draft

kevin: tl;dr: resolver returns resolution status + hotstart hint. hotstart gets invoked only when resolver signals 'ready-for-hotstart'. otherwise load is deferred and streamed.

sophia: this seems sane. main question: how do we surface partial-resolve errors vs transient IO errors? we need different SLO responses.

kevin: agree. plan is three resolution codes: OK, PARTIAL (meta present but blobs missing), NOTFOUND. PARTIAL maps to warmup-deferred + telemetry tag, NOTFOUND => immediate 404 to caller.

anya: minor nit: PARTIAL should include a 'missing-blob-list' small array so warmup planner can prioritize the subset to fetch first. cheap to emit.

miguel: +1. also want an escape hatch for latency-sensitive routes to force-eager-hotstart. config knob per route.

kevin: yep, routing policy will accept route-level override: `force_hotstart: true`. default false for general workloads.

rachel: operational question — how do we avoid thundering herd during deferred warmup? if many replicas see PARTIAL, they might all fetch the same shards.

kevin: proposed solution: coordinator issues a one-shot prefetch lease. first replica to claim the shard fetches and writes into shared ephemeral cache; others subscribe. lease TTL short (e.g., 5s).

infra-bot: deploy-check: checkpoint-resolver v0.3 feature-flagged on staging. tests: unit, integration against s3 mock, race-sim.

anya: sample config for the loader (proto):
```yaml
safeloader:
  resolve_mode: 'namespace-first'
  hotstart_policy: 'deferred'
  missing_blob_hint: true
  route_overrides:
    - route: '/chat/generative'
      force_hotstart: false
```

kevin: implementation notes: resolver should be sync and cheap — consult local index first, then sidecar if missing. avoid blocking on remote decompress/quant loads. warmup service handles heavy IO.

miguel: for safetensors shards we should include a per-shard checksum in the manifest so PARTIAL lists can be validated before attempting hotstart. helps with corrupt-blob fast-fail.

kevin: agreed. add checksum+size in manifest. also add a short follow-up: fallback policy for mismatched quant profiles (e.g., expected q4 but we only have q8) — plan to fall back to cpu-inference or alternate model version depending on route tier.

rachel: can we add a simple playbook for on-call? e.g., detection signals: repeated PARTIAL+lease-failures, spike in deferred-warmup latency, high mem-thrashing. actions: bump lease TTL, promote route to force_hotstart for emergency, rollback resolver flag.

kevin: i'll draft the playbook and add to the RFC. action items: 1) add missing_blob_list to PARTIAL (anya), 2) manifest checksums (miguel), 3) lease coordinator POC (kevin), 4) ops playbook draft (rachel).

anya: i'll do a small unit test that simulates interleaved PARTIAL + late-blob availability.

miguel: i'll wire checksum generation into the manifester pipeline.

kevin: thanks all. leaving staging flag on for two days. please post any regressions here. :eyes:
